org: University of Hawaii John A. Burns School of Medicine
applies_to: learners (medical and Imi Ho'ola students; residents and fellows of UH programs);faculty;staff
banned_uses: Generative AI tools must not be used to process, store, or transmit any sensitive information covered by HIPAA, FERPA, or other applicable data protection laws;all members of JABSOM must ensure that sensitive or potentially identifiable data is never input into open or unsecured AI platforms;any use of AI that promotes harm, violence, discrimination, or graphic or explicit content is prohibited;Not Permitted: generative AI to produce differential diagnoses, treatment plans, or other clinical reasoning outputs;AI tools should not be used to generate substantive content for assignments;Strictly Prohibited: the use of generative AI tools is not allowed for take-home exams, quizzes, or any assessments intended to measure individual knowledge and understanding;generative AI in simulations, virtual patient interactions, or clinical education scenarios is not allowed unless explicitly permitted by the instructor
permitted_uses: Students are permitted to use generative AI tools for academic assignments only as described in Appendix A, or otherwise if explicitly allowed by the instructor;grammar and syntax corrections, organizing existing information into outlines;faculty may use generative AI to collate and summarize qualitative comments on assessments and evaluations;faculty may use generative AI to create teaching materials including lecture notes and exam questions (permitted with disclosure)
phi_rule: Generative AI tools must not be used to process, store, or transmit any sensitive information covered by HIPAA, FERPA, or other applicable data protection laws; if there is a legitimate educational or research need to use AI tools with data derived from sensitive information, the data must first be deidentified to remove any personally identifiable information.
disclosure_rule: When AI tools are used to generate content for an assignment, students must include a clear disclosure statement indicating how and to what extent AI was utilized, placed at the beginning or end of the assignment as directed by the instructor; faculty must disclose AI use for generating lecture content, exam questions, or other educational resources; faculty model academic integrity by clearly stating their own use of AI tools.
assessment_rule: Faculty use of AI tools in assessing a learner's work is only permissible when such tools and their use uphold all relevant data privacy and security standards, professionalism, and due diligence; disclosure of AI use for summative comments carries over to subsequent documentation such as the MSPE.
secure_tools_named: ChatGPT (named in examples/disclosure statement); UH-licensed and approved LLMs (institution-specific, will not save or train on inputted student data)
enforcement: Any attempt to use AI tools to deceive or mislead will be treated as academic and professional misconduct; consequences may range from a failing grade on the assignment to more severe disciplinary action; consequences of misuse may include retraining, loss of access to AI tools, or more severe disciplinary actions; UH Executive Policy EP7.205 (Student Disciplinary Sanctions) and EP7.208 (Student Conduct Code).

org: Louisiana State University Health Sciences Center New Orleans
banned_uses: Students are prohibited from storing or transmitting protected health information (PHI) within AI tools, external cloud services, browser plug-ins, third-party integrations, or consumer applications unless formally vetted and approved by LSUHSC-NO's Information Security Office;students must never use generative AI as a substitute for their own knowledge acquisition, analysis or self-reflection;unless otherwise stated by the faculty member, upload of any course materials is not permitted;unauthorized use of AI tools to generate assignments or assessments constitutes academic misconduct
permitted_uses: Tools should be used with LSUHSC-NO credentials to ensure that privacy agreements apply;faculty and instructors have the authority and are encouraged to set and discuss specific guidelines regarding AI tool usage in their courses, assignments, or patient care work, including limitations on or encouraging use and uploading of course notes, slide decks, or other educational materials;students and faculty encouraged to participate in institution-sanctioned training
phi_rule: Always maintain academic integrity and never place any Protected Health Information (PHI) in non-approved AI tools to ensure that patient confidentiality and HIPAA regulations, and any applicable state or federal privacy regulations, are maintained.
secure_tools_named: Microsoft (OneDrive, Teams, and Copilot Chat);Zoom;Adobe Firefly (formal LSUHSC-NO licensing);ChatGPT (in citation example)
enforcement: Unauthorized use of AI tools to generate assignments or assessments constitutes academic misconduct and will be addressed in accordance with LSUHSC-NO Honor Code and relevant disciplinary procedures; students and faculty are responsible for the content they produce, regardless of AI assistance.

banned_uses: If you are trying to find a reference provided by ChatGPT, be aware that it may not exist.
assessment_rule: Students must be informed of AI course policies and under what circumstances they might responsibly use generative AI; for students in clinical situations or at off-site clinical locations, refer to the location's policy on AI use for clinical work.
enforcement: Any student's failure to comply with the statement on the use of generative AI tools in a course syllabus is considered a violation of academic integrity and subject to the same penalties stated in Rush University's Student Code of Conduct Policy (UAC0030) and the Academic Honesty Policy (UAC0031); disciplinary action imposed by the program/college.

org: University of Arkansas for Medical Sciences
banned_uses: Inputting identifiable participant data into public or non-secure AI tools is prohibited;instructors may not input any student-identifiable information or student work into GAI, plagiarism checking tools, or AI-detection software without explicit written permission from the student unless approved for use by UAMS;instructors are prohibited from asking students for permission to input their work into GAI without express permission from the AI Governance Committee;use of AI-based tools must not violate any copyright or intellectual property laws
permitted_uses: Use of GAI by students to satisfy course requirements must be authorized by the course faculty, trainer, or education supervisor;faculty describe whether GAI is prohibited, restricted (allowed for specific projects with appropriate citation), or unrestricted in a given course/activity;approved AI detection tools and GAI tools list available from the UAMS AI Governance Committee
phi_rule: When writing and entering queries into any GAI model outside of an electronic health record, PHI may only be inputted and processed by an AI or GAI tool if fully approved by UAMS AI Governance Committee and only when a fully executed BAA exists, compliant with UAMS Policy 2.1.23 Safeguarding Protected Health Information.
disclosure_rule: Faculty, employees, trainees, and academic visitors must fully disclose how and where they used GAI technology in their work (e.g., a statement in the methods or acknowledgements section); no disclosure required for Committee-approved tools, dictation, translation, spelling/grammar/punctuation, formatting, citation reformatting; investigators must clearly disclose in consent forms any use of generative AI tools when outputs could potentially re-identify research participants; clinicians must disclose whether patient consent was obtained before use of AI/GAI technology (if applicable).
assessment_rule: Any use of GAI by instructors to assist or review grading or evaluating student class assignments or work requires prior approval by the AI Governance Committee; any use of GAI to analyze student grades or other records also requires prior approval by the appropriate Dean and the UAMS Chancellor's AI Governance Committee; AI tools must be assessed by investigators for potential bias, especially in datasets involving human subjects.
secure_tools_named: UAMS AI Governance Committee-approved AI detection and GAI tools list
enforcement: Presentation of AI-generated work as one's own without appropriate attribution/citation is plagiarism, violating the UAMS Basic Code of Conduct, Responsible Conduct of Research policy, Student Code of Conduct, and Core Values; violations of this policy might be considered a violation of the College's Academic Misconduct/Integrity Policy and could include disciplinary action up to and including dismissal; AI-related disclosures or violations must be reported within 24 hours to the UAMS Chancellor's AI Governance Committee and the HIPAA Office / Office of Research Misconduct / TLS Committee / FERPA officer as appropriate; annual AI and GAI training required for all faculty, staff, and students.

org: University of Kentucky (UK ADVANCE; UK HealthCare)
banned_uses: UK ADVANCE recommends against using generative AI that is not housed within Epic, UK HealthCare's electronic health record management system, as well as other secure UKHC systems such as 3M and Hyland OnBase (esp. providing PHI including de-identified information, or making clinical decisions without appropriate expert and human oversight)
permitted_uses: Any rollout or integration of a generative AI tool within Epic and other secure UKHC systems will be reviewed and approved by the appropriate IT governance authorities in UKHC regarding risk and regulatory compliance; requests to integrate a third-party generative AI vendor go to the UKHC Demand Management Committee for review of security, safety, architecture, data, and privacy; Epic has laid out its Generative AI Roadmap.
phi_rule: Protected health information, personally identifiable information, other information protected by privacy laws, and any proprietary information should not be provided to generative AI tools unless they have been vetted for data privacy and other governance issues and approved by the University and UK HealthCare for the proposed use.
disclosure_rule: Transparency and explainability are important aspects of AI use in clinical care, yet it is difficult to explain how a generative AI tool arrived at its output from the given input; alignment involves accountability, autonomy, equity, integrity, morality, non-maleficence, privacy, security, transparency, and trust.
secure_tools_named: Epic EHR (generative AI housed within);3M;Hyland OnBase (secure UKHC systems)
enforcement: UK ADVANCE is taking an evidence-based approach with experts from many disciplines and continues to monitor experiences among our local campus and community as well as national and global developments.

org: University of Nevada Las Vegas Kirk Kerkorian School of Medicine (IT)
banned_uses: Personally identifiable information, system credentials (passwords, IP addresses), and non-public records should not be provided as prompts;using generative AI tools to complete a Financial or Human Capital Management project, or entering assignment or exam answers is not advisable;third-party tools are not supported by UNLV
permitted_uses: Enterprise tools are computer applications supported by UNLV that are designed to be scalable and integrated into university systems; check that the tool has robust security measures (encryption, secure data storage) to protect against unauthorized access and breaches; always employ human judgment when using AI outputs.
disclosure_rule: One should acknowledge the use of generative AI (other than incidental use) and default to disclosing such assistance when in doubt.
assessment_rule: Entering assignment or exam answers into generative AI tools is not advisable.

org: University of Nevada Reno School of Medicine
banned_uses: AI must not be used for the purpose of deidentifying protected health information, since datasets deidentified in this manner may be reverse engineered;meetings with legal counsel must not be transcribed;use of non-enterprise, commercially available generative AI platforms (e.g., ChatGPT Free or Plus) is discouraged due to their potential to retain and use inputted data
permitted_uses: Microsoft Copilot is UNR Med's approved AI tool and is strongly encouraged for AI-assisted work; all users intending to use generative AI for academic, clinical, or administrative tasks are encouraged to complete a brief institutional AI orientation module; users purchasing a subscription to non-enterprise AI platforms must complete the 'Restricted Use of Commercial AI Tools' agreement from Med IT
phi_rule: AI must not be used for the purpose of deidentifying protected health information, since datasets deidentified in this manner may be reverse engineered.
disclosure_rule: To the extent that the end-user relies substantially on the use of AI to produce original content, such use will be disclosed with the following statement: AI was used to generate this content, and the content was reviewed and edited for validity.
secure_tools_named: Microsoft Copilot (UNR Med's approved AI tool);ChatGPT;Claude;Gemini (non-Copilot tools require the UNR Med AI Attestation)
enforcement: If you choose to use a non-Copilot AI tool, completion of the UNR Med AI Attestation is required; policy references NSHE Records Retention Policy and the State Policy on the Responsible Use of AI.

org: University of Vermont Larner College of Medicine
banned_uses: Students cannot use generative AI tools to complete graded items (including readiness assurance tests and summative exams) unless explicitly permitted by faculty;AI-generated clinical documentation outside of supported EHR systems is prohibited;users must never enter NPPD (PHI, PII, and other data as defined in UVM's Privacy Policy) into an Open System;faculty-created materials may be uploaded to third party sites only with explicit approval by the faculty;content specifically commissioned and funded by the University requires institutional approval prior to uploading to third party sites
permitted_uses: Use of AI in developing self-study and self-assessment tools distinct from graded assessments is permitted;faculty may use generative AI to develop educational materials and student assignments (with disclosure);allowable AI use in clinical environments is primarily dictated by policies of the hosting facility;training in the use of generative AI in the educational environment is encouraged before implementation
phi_rule: Patient, student, or curricular data may only be input to Closed Compliant Systems; if FERPA or HIPAA data will be input, only use Closed Compliant System; protected patient health information may only be uploaded into HIPAA compliant applications that are supported by the hosting facility; when used, patient-specific health information must always be completely and rigorously de-identified prior to use as input in a generative AI tool; inputting NPPD into an open system is considered a breach of data security laws, such as HIPAA and the Vermont Data Breach Notification law.
disclosure_rule: In any assignment, students must disclose their use of generative AI tools in completion of assignments including reflections and case reports, specifying tools used; faculty must disclose their use of generative AI tools when developing educational materials and student assignments; faculty must disclose if AI products are used for analysis of student performance (e.g. OSCE or note review and feedback); when submitting scholarly work for publication or presentation, AI use must be reviewed and approved by the faculty advisor, adhere to venue requirements and must be disclosed, including the specific AI tool and how it was used.
assessment_rule: Students must author their own work and cannot use generative AI tools to complete graded items unless explicitly permitted by faculty; faculty are ultimately responsible for ensuring the accuracy of AI-generated results used in analysis of student performance; decisions influenced by AI must be subject to human review and human reviewers must have authority to override AI-generated outcomes; data generated from student activities (performance evaluations, assessments, course evaluations, narrative assignments, demographic information) may only be entered into secure COMTS approved closed systems.
secure_tools_named: UVM instance (system reviewed, approved and sanctioned by COMTS or UVM ETS); supported EHR systems; COMTS approved closed systems
enforcement: Use of AI in graded activities without permission and/or citation, and failure to disclose AI use, are against the Code of Academic Integrity and will be responded to in accordance with the Enforcement of University and Larner Behavioral Standards Policy; inputting NPPD into an open system requires notification to government oversight agencies and to the individual under HIPAA and the Vermont Data Breach Notification law.
